about: Kinds of good deed (Docs/Design/56-fame-and-memory.md, 1): each kind's weight (small, notable, great, legendary: how far word of it travels), its family (for nicknames), and its phrase, filled in when someone hears or tells of it ({beneficiary}: as the teller knows them; {place}: where; {detail}: what the source says). `perSeason` caps how many such deeds one wolf makes for one beneficiary in a season (0: no cap). Paid work is a deed only where a kind here says so. Deeds pay nothing.

kinds.phrase: drove the bandits off the road at {place}
saw a caravan safely through to {place}
helped the watch catch a thief in {place}

word.about: How far a notable or greater deed has got round its town (doc 56, 2): its reach starts at `start` and is all over town in `days`; carried by a caravan it starts at `caravanStart` and grows at half speed; a legendary one starts at `legendStart` everywhere. It holds fresh for `fresh` days, then fades to nothing over `fade`. A town's word holds at most `most` deeds. `ears`: how much more (or less) than others each sort of resident hears.
